messages:
sanjay: quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick an approach for RBAC enforcement on console queries. two paths: pushdown to query layer (DB filters) or enforce in console after full result sets. both have tradeoffs on latency/cost and correctness.

julia: recap from the RFC: pushdown means generate paramized filters per user/route and let the query service include `team_id`/`project_id` predicates. console-side enforcement means broader queries + post-filtering; simpler but lots of traffic and cache misses.

kevin: numbers from the perf run yesterday: naive post-filtering increased 95p latency by ~220ms for dashboard endpoints under 200rps baseline. cost estimate was ~1.9x for DB CPU in worst-case tenant skew. :grimacing:

maria: big worry with pushdown is combinatorial predicate explosion for shared dashboards. if we generate per-user `IN (...)` clauses we lose cacheability. also SQL plan variability. example we saw: 
```sql
SELECT ts, value FROM metrics WHERE metric = 'latency' AND team_id IN (:teams) AND ts >= $start
```
When :teams is large, plan goes bad.

julia: alternative hybrid: push down coarse tenant filters (e.g., org_id or shard_id) to keep DB scans small, but do resource-intense fine-grained checks in the query layer via lightweight tag-filtering and short-circuit deny for obvious mismatches. keep per-route prepared statements but avoid expanding huge `IN` lists.

sanjay: i like hybrid. also add sampling-based pre-agg for heavy panels so we avoid full scans for 90% of traffic. we can expose a query-mode flag on routes: `mode=fast|exact` so product can choose.

kevin: implementation notes: 1) extend query proxy to accept `auth_filters` meta header (json blob) instead of literal SQL injection. 2) proxy translates meta into either paramized predicate or runtime tag-check middleware. prevents plan explosion. 3) add a planner heuristic: if `teams` length > 20, switch to tag-filtering path.

maria: don't forget audit logs + determinism tests. we should have a test harness that replays real dashboard queries and asserts identical final result set between old and hybrid mode for a 2-week sample (within tolerance). also a regression alert on 99p latency.

julia: rollout proposal: canary config on Dedicated first (50% capacity) -> simulate tenant skew -> enable on Hosted with 5% of traffic -> bump to 25% after 48h if no SLO regressions -> full. add feature-flag for `mode=fast` per-route.

sanjay: action items: kevin to prototype `auth_filters` header + planner switch, maria to own replay harness and regression alerts, julia to draft canary runbook and SLIs. i'll shepherd the design doc updates.

kevin: started a branch at github.com/redwood-inference/console-query/proposals/auth-filter-proxy, will post a short demo by EOD. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary job created: console-query-authfilter-canary-2026-03-20 (id: cj-9834). logs will appear in #eng-ops.
